title: Aloo Masala

overview.description: Soft potatoes cooked with onion, mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric and gentle spices.

ingredients: 800g potatoes, peeled and cut into medium chunks
method: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender but not falling apart.
Drain the potatoes and allow them to steam dry for a few minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or kadai.
When they begin to pop, add the cumin seeds and curry leaves.
Add the sliced onion and cook until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and green chillies.
Add the turmeric, ground cumin and ground coriander.
Add the cooked potatoes and salt.
Gently stir until the potatoes are coated in the spices.
Cook for 5–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes have absorbed the flavours.

learning.did-you-know: Aloo means potato in several South Asian languages, while masala generally refers to a mixture of spices or a spiced preparation. Aloo masala can therefore refer to many different spiced potato dishes.
learning.what-you-will-learn: How whole spices are tempered in hot oil to release their aroma and how spices can transform a simple potato into a flavourful dish.

notes.why-its-in-the-chapman-kitchen: A versatile potato dish that can be served as a filling, side dish or simple meal and makes good use of familiar pantry spices.
chapman-tips: Don't overcook the potatoes during boiling or they may break apart in the pan.
Allowing the potatoes to steam dry helps them absorb the spices without becoming watery.
Mustard seeds should be added to hot oil and allowed to pop before adding other ingredients.
The lemon juice at the end helps balance the richness and spices.
For a drier dosa filling, break some of the potatoes apart as they cook.
For a chunkier side dish, stir very gently and keep the potato pieces intact.
Fresh coriander can be replaced with a little fresh curry leaf if desired.
notes.batch-cooking: Good for batch cooking. Cool thoroughly before refrigerating or freezing. The texture may soften slightly after freezing and reheating.
notes.leftovers: Leftover aloo masala can be used as a filling for dosa, paratha, sandwiches, wraps or samosas.
